purpose: Chain coverage of the paid Nansen provider, per capability. Derived from the COMMITTED OpenAPI spec at zero credits; a single live call confirms the spec has not drifted.

method.rule: A COMPOSITE capability is covered by the INTERSECTION of its sub-calls, never the union. smart-money.flows issues /smart-money/netflow (17 chains) AND /tgm/holders (25); the union would add chains where the first sub-call succeeds, the second is refused, and the credits for the first are already spent (the DF-1 failure class).
method.recorded_deviation: R-58a asks for 'a run with the key'. The spec already carries the fact per endpoint, so a full live sweep of 25 chains would spend credits to reach the same conclusion. Spec + one spot-check meets the requirement's intent more strictly than its letter.

half_succeeding_chains.note: Covered for token.risk but NOT for smart-money.flows — exactly what a union would have wrongly claimed.
half_succeeding_chains.why_the_two_numbers_differ: 'hyperevm' and 'hyperliquid' are two VENDOR tokens for one chain of ours (hyperliquid-l1), and that chain IS covered for smart-money.flows via 'hyperevm'. Counting in vendor tokens overstates our exposure by one.

live_spot_check.why_this_chain: outside the M2 pair (ethereum/solana) — the point is to prove the spec's widening is real, not to re-verify what already worked
live_spot_check.result: HTTP 200 with populated token_info + risk/reward indicators

vendor_token_mapping.note: registry.data.json vendors.nansen holds the VENDOR's token, not our slug.

degraded_path: With no NANSEN_API_KEY the spot-check is skipped, coverage still comes from the spec, and the state is 'spec-only' — unverified, NEVER 'unsupported' (R-58d): a false narrowing is as wrong as a false widening.
